<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par165 />ing, where we should expect a final clause (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=9}} ''then I commanded, and they cleansed'', equivalent to ''that they should cleanse, and they cleansed''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=7}} a negative final clause is connected in this way by {{GHGheb|text=וְלאֹ}}), cf. {{GHGpar|120|f}}.

For examples of the direct subordination of the final imperfect (without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}) see {{GHGpar|120|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|165|b}}
'''2.''' Final conjunctions are {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן אֲשֶׁר|translate=to the end that}}; also simply {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=6}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲבוּר אֲשֶׁר}} prop. ''for the purpose that'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=10}}, and simply {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲבוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=20|hidebook=1}}; also the simple {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=27}} a final clause is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אֵת אֲשֶׁר}}, thus at the same time taking the form of an object-clause.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=10}}, 40, 6:3, 32:46, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=14}} f.; negatively, {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=16}}; or {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ ּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=14}}; also negatively, {{GHGheb|text=עַל־דִּבְרַת שֶׁלֹּא}} ''for the matter (purpose) that'' ... ''not'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי}} with imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=14}} ''that'' ... ''not''.—Quite exceptional is the use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} (if the text be right) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=מִן־יְקוּמוּן}}, with the imperfect, equivalent to ''that'' ... ''not'' [in prose, {{GHGheb|text=מִקּוּם}}].

{{GHGmargin-letter|165|c}}
Rem. All the conjunctions here mentioned are naturally always used with the imperfect, see {{GHGpar|107|q}} (on the apparent exception in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=24}}, see {{GHGpar|74|g}}).—On the negative conjunctions {{GHGheb|text=אַל}} and {{GHGheb|text=פֶּן|translate=that not, lest}}, see {{GHGpar|152|f}} and w. On the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} as a supposed conjunction (equivalent to the Arabic ''li'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=19}}, see {{GHGpar|66|i}}.</ref> (also {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, &c.) as the equivalent of a final clause ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, &c.), see {{GHGpar|114|f}}, h, p. On the continuation of such infinitival constructions by means of the finite verb, see {{GHGpar|114|r}}. On the negation of the final infinitive by {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי}}, {{GHGpar|114|s}}. On the preposition {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} with a substantive or infinitive as the equivalent of a negative final clause ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=23}}, &c.), see {{GHGpar|119|x}} and y.<section end=par165 />

<section begin=par166 />{{GHGpar-heading|166|Consecutive Clauses}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|166|a}}
'''1.''' Consecutive clauses are added by means of simple {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}} with the jussive,<ref>That such examples as {{GHGheb|text=וִיֽכַזֵּב}} are to be regarded as jussive is probable from the analogy of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=10}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=33}}.</ref> especially after negative and interrogative sentences, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אִישׁ אֵל וִיֽכַזֵּב וּבֶן־אָדָם וְיִתְנֶחָ֑ם|translate=God is not a man, that he should lie, and}} (i.e. neither) ''the son of man, that he should repent''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=וְנֶחְמְדֵ֫הוּ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=מִי חָכָם וְיָבֵן אֵ֫לֶּה נָבוֹן וְיֵֽדָעֵם|translate=who is wise, that he may understand these things? prudent, that he may know them?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא}}=''so that'' ... ''not''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} is separated from the predicate by the object. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=10}} a negative consecutive clause comes after a cohortative, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=5}} after a perfect consecutive.—On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=32}}, 33 the jussive in the sense of a consecutive clause is attached without {{GHGterm|Wāw}} to the preceding negative sentence (in<section end=par166 /><noinclude>
